newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish drive into north Iraq not imminent- Ciller.
newsitem.headline: Turkish drive into north Iraq not imminent- Ciller.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Thursday that a military thrust into northern Iraq was not imminent, despite military threats to root out Kurdish separatist rebel bases there.
"What is on the agenda is not an operation. What is on the agenda is not to allow such (rebel) infiltrations," Ciller told reporters as she left the foreign ministry. She did not elaborate.
A high-ranking military official told Reuters earlier that Turkish troops, backed by air power, could attack Kurdish separatist rebels in northern Iraq.

Witnesses said heavy military preparations were in progress near Turkey's porous border with Iraq. The stepped-up activity followed Ankara's announcement that it was preparing to set up a security cordon inside northern Iraq to halt Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) infiltration.

A foreign ministry spokesman said the zone would be five to 10 km (three to six miles) deep, but Ciller refused to go into details. "We could think of the security cordon like this -- it will not be permitted for the PKK to mass on Turkey's borders or infiltrate," she said.
